title: Finite Q3 cutoff scaling of the raw commutator-sum Trotter coefficient
question: When the registered finite Q3 oscillator cutoff is varied at fixed volume and source fixture, how does the raw operator-norm commutator coefficient entering the Lie-Trotter bound scale, and does this finite audit provide a cutoff-independent coefficient?

adversarial_review.check: Each row reconstructs the oscillator and every local Q3 term from the declared cutoff; no n=3 value is reused as a derived number.
Overlapping commutators are evaluated on their union support and disjoint supports are exactly zero; one full tensor embedding is checked against the local norm.
The coefficient is explicitly the bounded raw operator-norm coefficient; no energy/state-weighted estimate is silently substituted or promoted.
Growth ratios and monotonicity are diagnostics over the declared finite cutoff list only; they are not an asymptotic divergence theorem.
The physical fixture and graph volumes are inherited by manifest chain; no source, beta, volume, or exhaustion uniformity is inferred.
Finite cutoff rows do not establish a common unbounded domain, thermodynamic histories, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, or Pre-A closure.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks exact rational scaling bookkeeping and the fixed-step coefficient identity; matrix norms, cutoff asymptotics, unbounded domains and all QFT limits remain Python/open analysis.

qft_interface.closed: A reproducible finite-cutoff table for the raw commutator-sum coefficient and its induced fixed-step Trotter/history coefficients is obtained for the inherited Q3 fixture.
qft_interface.open: A cutoff-independent raw operator-norm coefficient, energy/state-weighted replacement, common domain, thermodynamic history, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 evidence only; no TECT production owner, physical-empty reference or Sector-A closure is supplied.

no_overclaim: This package is a finite cutoff-scaling audit. It records a route-local boundary for the raw bounded-operator-norm coefficient and does not prove its infinite-cutoff behavior or any QFT, C6, Sector A, Pre-A, or Clay result.
